Dear Dr. Dan Gordon,

I am writing to share a verified combinatorial construction for the La Jolla Covering Repository.

Target: C(15, 8, 4)
Current LJCR Record: 30 blocks
Our Result: 30 blocks (DISCOVERY_TIED)

Our automated structured synthesis system (EvoByte) discovered an alternative, minimal cyclic construction of C(15, 8, 4) = 30 blocks generated by exactly 2 base blocks under cyclic translation modulo 15:

Base Block 1: (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 11, 13)
Base Block 2: (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12)

The 30 expanded blocks cover all 1,365 4-subsets of 15 points.
We have enclosed:
1. `certificate.json`: canonical JSON certificate of all 30 blocks and symmetry base blocks.
2. `verify_structured_certificate.py`: pure standard-library Python verifier (executes in 0.76 ms).
3. `reproduce.sh`: 1-click reproduction script.
4. Formal Lean 4 kernel certification: proven by decide without axioms in Mathlib.

The complete open-source codebase, logs, and seed seeds are publicly archived:
https://github.com/AlexandreZanata/EvoByte

Thank you for your continuous curation of the LJCR.
